THIS MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT (this "Agreement") is made and entered into this day of August, 2018, by and between Lockton Management, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company having its registered office at 444 West 47th Street, Suite 900, Kansas City, Missouri 64112(hereinafter the "Customer"), and Larsen & Toubro Infotech Limited a company incorporated under the laws of India and having its corporate office at L&T Technology Centre, Gate No.5, Saki Vihar Road, Powai, Mumbai 400 072, India through its branch located at 2035 Lincoln Highway, Suite 3000, Edison Square West, Edison-NJ 08817having its office (hereinafter referred to as "Service Provider")

WHEREAS, Customer desires to engage Service Provider or its affiliate, for self and/or on its behalf for its affiliate(s), from time to time pursuant to one or more Work Order(s) to provide information technology Services including consulting, programming, application development, implementation, support Services and related Services and Service Provider is interested in accepting such engagements, subject to the parties' further agreement on the scope and terms of each such Work Order; and
WHEREAS, Customer and Service Provider mutually desire to set forth in this Agreement certain terms applicable to all such engagements;
NOW, THEREFORE, Customer and Service Provider, intending to be legally bound, hereby agree as follows:
1 Work order

The scope and description of Services to be provided by Service Provider and specific deliverables, if any to be created and provided to Customer as part of the Services such Services and deliverables hereinafter referred as "Services" and "Deliverables” respectively will be mutually agreed and set forth in individual Work Order ("Work Order"). Each Work Order for Services provided on time and material basis that may be executed by the Parties under this Agreement will be substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit A. Each Work Order for Services provided on fixed price basis that may be executed by the Parties under this Agreement will be substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit B. Any Work Order, when executed by both Parties shall be deemed to incorporate the provisions of this Agreement. Further, in performing the Services hereunder Service Provider may utilize the personnel, resources and facilities of its affiliates and other long term sourcing associates provided that in all such cases Service Provider remains fully responsible and liable for the performance of Services and as between Customer and Service Provider, with respect to each individual assigned by Service Provider to perform the Services.
2 Contract administration
2.1 Contract Coordinator
Each party designates the following individuals as their respective Contract Coordinators:
Customer: Said Taiym, Executive Vice President, Chief Digital Officer
Service Provider: Anil Vazirani, Chief Business Officer

The Contract Coordinators of each party shall be responsible for arranging all meetings, visits, and consultations between the parties that are of a non-technical nature. The Contract Coordinators shall also be responsible for receiving all notices under this Agreement and for all administrative matters such as invoices, payments, and amendments.
2.2 Issuance of Work Orders
The format of the Work Order is attached herewith as Exhibit A. The initial Work Order(s), as per the format in Exhibit A, agreed to by the parties are set forth as attachments to this Agreement.
3 Changes

Changes in any Work Order or in any of the Services or Deliverables (as defined in the applicable Work Order) under any Work Order shall become effective only when a written change request is executed by authorized representatives of both parties
4 Notice of delay

Service Provider agrees to notify Customer promptly of any factor, occurrence, or event coming to its attention that may affect Service Provider's ability to meet the requirements of any Work Order issued under this Agreement or that is likely to occasion any material delay in delivery of Deliverables. Service Provider shall not be responsible for and Service Provider shall be excused of and shall have no liability resulting from any failure to meet the timetable and deadlines or for failure to perform its obligations set out in the Work Order caused by anything done or failed to be done by Customer, its service providers and or its agents, and all dates by which Service Provider is required to perform any obligation under the Work Order will be deemed to be changed to a subsequent date determined by the Parties, each acting reasonably and taking into account the availability of the required Service Provider resources, and such change (including the additional cost, if any, payable by Customer as a result of such delay) shall be implemented pursuant to mutually agreed change control process.
5 Compensation
5.1 Basis of Compensation
The compensation payable by Customer to Service Provider for all Services to be performed and Deliverables to be delivered shall be set forth in each applicable Work Order.
5.2 Rate Revision

The rates for the Services performed by the Service Provider for the Customer on time and material basis shall be set forth in Exhibit C to this Agreement. The rates provided by Service Provider are valid for a period of 1 year from the Effective Date and thereafter will be subject to revision at each anniversary date. The prices may be modified taking into account a cost of living adjustment formula. The Cost of Living adjustment formula shall be as follows:
P1 = PO x (Price Country Index 1 / Price Country Index 0)
1. PO = current price at the date of signature of the present Agreement
2. P1 = new price at the date of rate revision
3. Price Country Index 0 = consumer price index value for a specific country for the month of signature of the present Agreement
4. Price Country Index 1 = consumer price index value for a specific country on the date of rate revision

"Price Country Index" means, with respect to each country, a figure that reflects the change, if any, in the specific consumer price index taken for that country for that 12-month period as published by that country's official department of statistics or any other appropriate indices as mutually agreed upon.
5.3 Expenses:

The Service Provider will provide standard configuration PCs with standard softwares to the offshore consultants. Any special software that may be required at offshore to perform the Services will be provided by the Customer. At onsite, the Customer will provide any equipment (PC, access to phone, fax, email, printer etc.) and office space which is required to perform the Services by Service Provider's personnel.
Each Work Order will specify a location of performance of Services. Any local travel to other location than the location mentioned will be charged with prior approval to the Customer at actual.
All the reasonable out of pocket expenses incurred by the Service Provider in the course of rendering Service to the Customer under this Agreement will be reimbursed by Customer at actuals.
For instance, expenses incurred when travelling from the Service Provider's base locations will be borne by the Customer if the duration of the assignment is less than three months.
5.4 Taxes

The fees payable to Service Provider are exclusive of all service, use, value added tax or taxes of similar nature and Customer shall be responsible to pay the amount of such taxes that it owes. Each party is responsible for its own income taxes.
6 Working hours
- Normal Working Hours shall mean the 8 working hours per day between 8 am to 8 pm local time for onsite on weekdays (excluding weekends and holidays).
- Normal Working Hours shall mean the 9 working hours per day between 8.30 am to 8.30 pm local time for offshore on weekdays (excluding weekends and holidays)

- Any additional work which needs extra working hours (only beyond normal working hours, holidays, Saturdays or Sundays) will be charged at the rate of 1.5 times the normal hourly rate. Extra working hours can only be worked and billed with prior written approval of the Lockton.
7 Invoicing

Service Provider shall submit invoices to Customer for Services and/or Deliverables at such time or times as payment becomes due under each Work Order. Invoices that are not disputed shall be payable within 30 days from the receipt of the invoice. Invoices shall be submitted no more frequently than monthly for charges due or accruing in each calendar month. All invoices shall specifically refer to the Work Order to which they relate. Whenever an invoice includes charges for time and materials, the invoice shall indicate the names and hours of the personnel performing the work. Each invoice shall separately set forth travel expenses, if any, authorized by Customer for reimbursement. Supporting documentation (e.g., receipts for air travel, hotels, and rental cars) called for by Customer's standard reimbursement policies (which shall be informed to the Service Provider prior to beginning of any assignment under this Agreement) shall accompany any such invoice. For non-disputed invoice payments not made within the aforesaid period of 30 days, Service Provider will without prejudice to any other remedies that it may have in this regard charge interest @1.5% per month calculated from the date the payment became due until the recovery is made in full with interest. If an invoice is disputed, Customer shall pay the amount of an agreed-upon invoice within thirty (30) days of when the parties agree upon the invoice. Without prejudice to the other rights available, Service Provider also reserves the right to withhold the provision of Services till such time all the payments due to it under this Agreement have been made by Customer and any such withholding by Service Provider shall not be treated as breach by it of the provisions of this Agreement.
8 Reports
8.1 Monthly Reports

Service Provider agrees to provide to Customer reports of the progress of the work required under each Work Order issued hereunder, any anticipated problems (resolved or unresolved), and any indication of delay in fixed or tentative schedules. The frequency of submission of reports to the Customer shall be as mutually agreed between the parties in the respective Work Orders.
8.2 Progress Review

Approximately once every four weeks, the parties shall meet for a formal progress presentation, during which Service Provider's management shall describe the status of the work required under each Work Order issued hereunder. Such presentation shall provide projections of the time of completion, and the status of Service Provider's Services and Deliverables, and shall address any problems that have come to Service Provider's attention and Service Provider's views as to how such problems may be resolved.
8.3 Site Visits

Service Provider shall upon reasonable notice (at least 48 business hours), allow access to its premises by Customer for purposes of design review, "walkthroughs," and discussions between Customer and Service Provider's management and personnel concerning the status and conduct of work being performed under any Work Orders issued hereunder. The representatives of Customer visiting Service Provider's premises shall comply with Service Provider's confidentiality and security policies applicable to such premises.
9 Delivery and acceptance

Service Provider shall deliver all Deliverables (in accordance with the applicable Work Order), upon completion, to Customer for testing and acceptance. Unless a different procedure for testing and acceptance is set forth in a Work Order, Customer shall immediately commence acceptance testing following its receipt of the Deliverables. Upon completion of such testing, Customer shall issue to Service Provider notice of acceptance or rejection of the Deliverables within a reasonable time but not later than 5 business days. In the event of rejection, Customer shall give its reasons for rejection to Service Provider in reasonable detail. Service Provider shall use all reasonable effort to correct any deficiencies or nonconformities and resubmit the rejected items for acceptance testing and the foregoing procedure shall be repeated until the acceptance is complete. Customer agrees that once the Deliverables have been accepted by the Customer, the Customer will not raise any quality related issues with respect to such accepted Deliverables. Notwithstanding the foregoing the Deliverables shall be deemed to be accepted if: (a) the Service Provider does not receive any notice of acceptance or rejection within the time limit specified herein above, or (b) Customer starts using the Deliverables in a live production environment (other than as part of agreed review and acceptance testing procedure, such as UAT). The provisions of this section shall apply only in the case of Services undertaken on a Fixed Price basis.

Service Provider shall have no liability or obligation under this Section 10 for the delay in completing acceptance tests or failure of the acceptance tests if such delay or failure is determined to be due to reasons not attributable to the Service Provider. The correction or reworking of the Deliverables and all related activities shall be at the cost of Service Provider if the failure is determined to be due to reasons solely attributable to Service Provider. In all other cases, any additional costs, charges or expenses incurred by Service Provider in correcting or reworking the relevant Deliverables shall be to the account of Customer and Customer shall reimburse to Service Provider such costs charges or expenses.

Notwithstanding the fact that the acceptance or rejection of the Deliverables are not communicated by the Customer to the Service Provider within the stipulated time the Customer is hereby obligated not to withhold or reject payments for the Deliverables to the Service Provider.
10 Ownership and rights
10.1 Ownership of Work Product by Customer

Subject to Section 10.2 below Service Provider agrees that all Deliverables created or developed by Service Provider specifically for the Customer, shall be the sole and exclusive property of Customer provided all the payments due to Service Provider for the Deliverables rendered under the Work Order pursuant to this Agreement have already been paid by the Customer to the Service Provider. Service Provider hereby assigns to Customer all right, title and interest in and to such Deliverables developed exclusively for the Customer and identified in the relevant Work Order, whether or not such Deliverables are deemed "works made for hire" under the relevant laws. Upon Customer's written request and expense, Service Provider shall execute and deliver to Customer all instruments and other documents, and shall take, at Customer's costs, such other reasonable actions as may be necessary or reasonably requested by Customer and as may be necessary to give effect to the Customer's proprietary rights in such Deliverables.
10.2 Service Provider Pre-Existing IP and Third Party Materials

Customer acknowledges that in performing Services under this Agreement Service Provider may use Service Provider's proprietary materials including without limitation any software (or any part or component thereof), tools, methodology, processes, ideas, know-how and technology that are or were developed or owned by Service Provider prior to or independent of the Services performed hereunder or any improvements, enhancements, modifications or customization made thereto as part of or in the course of performing the Services hereunder, ("Service Provider Pre-Existing IP"). Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in this Agreement, Service Provider shall continue to retain all the ownership, the rights title and interests to all Service Provider Pre-Existing IP and nothing contained herein shall be construed as preventing or restricting Service Provider from using Service Provider Pre-Existing IP in any manner.

To the extent that any Service Provider Pre-Existing IP or a portion thereof is incorporated or contained in a Deliverable under a Work Order under this Agreement, Service Provider hereby grants to Customer a non- exclusive, perpetual, royalty free, fully paid up, irrevocable license, with the right to sublicense, to use, copy, install, perform, display, modify and create derivative works of any such Service Provider Pre-Existing IP in connection with the Deliverables and only as part of the Deliverables in which they are incorporated or embedded. The foregoing license does not authorizes Customer to (a) separate Service Provider Pre-Existing IP from the Deliverable in which they are incorporated for creating a standalone product for marketing to others; (b) independently sell, lease, exchange, mortgage, pledge, license, sub license, assign or in any other way convey, transfer or alienate the Service Provider Pre-Existing IP in favor of any person, and/or (c) reverse compile or in any other way arrive at or attempt to arrive at the source code of the Service Provider Pre- Existing IP. All the third-party materials shall be governed by the terms of the respective third party end user license agreement (EULA).
10.3 Residuary Rights

Each party shall be entitled to use in the normal course of its business and in providing same or similar Services or development of similar deliverables for its other clients, the general knowledge and experience gained and retained in the unaided human memory of its personnel in the performance of this Agreement and Work Order(s) hereunder. For the purposes of clarity Service Provider shall be free to provide any Services or design any deliverable(s) that perform functions same or similar to the Deliverables being provided hereunder for Customer, for any other client or customer of Service Provider. Nothing contained in this Section shall relieve either party of its confidentiality obligations with respect to the proprietary and confidential information or material of the other party.
11 Representations and warranties

Each party warrants that it has the right and power to enter into this Agreement and an authorized representative has executed this Agreement. Each party represents and warrants that it is compliance and will remain in compliance with applicable laws and regulations applicable to the Services provided hereunder. Service Provider warrants that the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner in accordance with recognized industry standards. Customer represents that it owns or has properly licensed the materials supplied to Service Provider for the performance of Services hereunder.

Except as set forth in this Section 11 either party makes no warranties to other party, express or implied, with respect to any Services or Deliverables provided hereunder or under any Work Order, including, without limitation, any implied warranties of merchantability or fitness for a particular purpose. All such other warranties are hereby disclaimed.
12 Confidential information

Each party (in such capacity, the "Receiving Party") acknowledges and agrees to maintain the confidentiality of Confidential Information (as hereafter defined) provided by the other party (in such capacity, the "Disclosing Party") hereunder or under any Work Order. The Receiving Party shall not disclose or disseminate the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information to any person other than those employees, agents, contractors, subcontractors and licensees of the Receiving Party, or its affiliates, who have a need to know it in order to assist the Receiving Party in performing its obligations, or to permit the Receiving Party to exercise its rights under this Agreement or any Work Order. In addition, the Receiving Party (i) shall take all reasonable steps to prevent unauthorized access to the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information, and (ii) shall not use the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information, or authorize other persons or entities to use the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information, for any purposes other than in connection with performing its obligations or exercising its rights hereunder or under any Work Order. As used herein, “reasonable steps" means steps that a party takes to protect its own, similarly confidential or proprietary information of a similar nature, which steps shall in no event be less than a reasonable standard of care.

The term "Confidential Information", as used herein, shall mean all non-public information shared between the parties, including without limitation, financial information, compensation information, business strategies, plans and procedures, proprietary information, software, tools, processes, methodologies, data and trade secrets, and other confidential information and materials of the Disclosing Party, its affiliates, their respective clients or suppliers, or other persons or entities with whom they do business, that may be obtained by the Receiving Party from any source or that may be developed for the Disclosing Party as a result of this Agreement. Confidential Information also includes protected health information, electronic or otherwise, that is protected by state privacy laws and/or the federal Health Information Portability and Accountability Act of 1996, as amended, and the regulations enacted pursuant to it and its amendments, including but not limited to 45 C.F.R. § 160.103; all other medical or health information; and, personal private information, electronic or otherwise, that is protected by law, including but not limited to federal, or state privacy laws.

The provisions of this Section 12 respecting Confidential Information shall not apply to the extent, but only to the extent, that such Confidential Information is: (a) previously known to the Receiving Party at the time of disclosure, or (b) independently developed by the receiving party without reference to Confidential Information of the Disclosing Party, (c) disclosed to the receiving party by a third party without an obligation of confidentiality, or (d) already in or subsequently comes into the public domain (other than as a result of a breach of this Agreement); (e) required to be disclosed by the Receiving Party by law, regulation, court order or other legal process. Should the Receiving Party disclose the Confidential Information to any third party pursuant to subsection 12(e), it shall cooperate in attempting to provide the Confidential Information in such a manner (by editing or redacting the Confidential Information in lieu of disclosing the complete Confidential Information) so that the Disclosing Party's privilege or competitive advantage will not be compromised.
13 Indemnification
13.1 Infringement Indemnity

A. Service Provider will defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its directors, officers and employees (each, a "Customer Indemnified Party"), from and against any third-party suit, proceeding, judgment, costs and expenses (including, reasonable attorney fees) to the extent based on allegation that the Services or Deliverables as provided to Customer by Service Provider and the use thereof by Customer as contemplated in the Agreement or applicable Work Order constitutes an infringement of or misappropriation of the copyright, patent, trademark or trade secret rights of any third party (each, an "Infringement Claim"). Service Provider shall have no obligations with respect to any Infringement Claims to the extent that the Infringement Claim arises or results from: (i) Service Provider's compliance with Customer's specific technical designs or instructions; (ii) inclusion in a Deliverable of any content or other materials provided by Customer and the infringement relates to or arises from such Customer materials or provided material; (iii) modification of a Deliverable after delivery by Service Provider to Customer if such modification was not made by or on behalf of the Service Provider; (iv) operation or use of some or all of the Deliverable in combination with products, information, specification, instructions, data, materials not provided by Service Provider; or (v) use of the Deliverables for any purposes for which the same have not been designed or developed or other than in accordance with any applicable specifications or documentation provided under the applicable Work Order by the Service Provider; or (vi) use of a superseded release of some or all of the Deliverables or Customer's failure to use any modification of the Deliverable furnished under this Agreement including, but not limited to, corrections, fixes, or enhancements made available by the Service Provider.

B. Customer will defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Service Provider, applicable Service Provider affiliates ("Service Provider Indemnified Party") from and against any third party suit, proceedings damages, judgments, cost and expenses (including reasonable attorney fees) relating to any infringement claim by a third party to the extent based on any Customer materials provided to Service Provider by or on behalf of Customer or the access and use by Service Provider of any Customer provided software or material in connection with Service Provider's performance of Services hereunder without breaching the terms of this Agreement.
13.2 Additional Obligation of Service Provider

In the event that Customer is enjoined or otherwise prohibited, or is reasonably likely to be enjoined or otherwise prohibited, from using any Deliverable as a result of or in connection with any claim for which Service Provider is required to indemnify Customer under Section 13 according to a final decision of the courts or in the view of Service Provider, Service Provider, may at its own expense and option: (i) procure for Customer the right to continue using such Deliverable; (ii) modify the Deliverable so that it becomes non- infringing without materially altering its capacity or performance; (iii) replace the Deliverable with work product that is equal in capacity and performance but is non-infringing; or (iv) If such measures do not achieve the desired result and if the infringement is established by a final decision of the courts or a judicial or extrajudicial settlement, the Service Provider shall refund the Customer the fees effectively paid for that Deliverable by the Customer.
13.3 Mutual Indemnification for Certain Claims

Each party (in the capacity as Indemnifying Party) will defend, indemnify and hold the other party, its affiliates, directors, officers and employees (in the capacity of Indemnified Party) from and against any cost and expenses arising out of or related to the Indemnifying Party's actual or alleged breach of (i) confidentiality obligation under Section 12; (ii) representation and warranties under Section 11 and any third party claims for breach of material obligation imposed by this Agreement; and (iii) gross negligence, willful misconduct and fraud,.
13.4 Additional Provisions for Indemnification

A party shall not be entitled to seek any indemnification from the other party unless such party (i) provides the other party with reasonable prompt written notice of any claim, such that the Indemnifying Party is not materially prejudiced due to the timing of the notice, demand or action for which such party is seeking or may seek indemnification hereunder and gives the indemnifying party the right to have sole control over the defense and settlement negotiations; (ii) does not make any statement or admission in relation to such claim which may prejudicially affect the chances of settlement or defense of such claim; (iii) reasonably cooperate with the indemnifying party in assisting the defense of the claim and in the negotiations or settlements of any such claim, demand or action by providing all assistance and information to perform the above obligations; and (iv) allow the other party, at its own expense, exclusively defend such litigation, negotiations and settlements with counsel of its own choosing. The Indemnifying Party shall not have the right to settle any claim if such settlement contains a stipulation to, or an admission or acknowledgement of, any wrongdoing (whether in tort or otherwise) on the part of the indemnified party.
14 Limitation of Liability

Neither party shall be liable to the other for any special, indirect, incidental, consequential (including loss of profit or revenue), exemplary or punitive damages whether in contract, tort or other theories of law, even if such party has been advised of the possibility of such damages.

Except for a breach of confidentiality obligation under section 12, breach of representation and warranty under section 11 or gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud or intellectual property infringement claim, the total liability of either party arising from or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed 1.5 times the fees paid or payable to the Service Provider for a twelve month period pursuant to the Work Order giving rise to such liability.
15 Term and termination
15.1 Term of Agreement

This Agreement shall be effective upon the date specified at the beginning hereof ("Effective Date") and shall remain in force for a period of one (1) year, unless otherwise terminated as provided herein. However, this Agreement shall continue to remain in effect with respect to any Work Orders already issued hereunder at the time of such termination, until such Work Orders are themselves terminated or performance thereunder is completed. The Agreement shall auto renew unless either party provides notice to the other party of its intent to terminate the agreement on not less than sixty days' prior written notice.
15.2 Termination of Work Orders

Customer may, at its sole option, terminate any or all Work Orders outstanding, or any portion thereof, upon 90 days' written notice. Service Provider shall be paid for the Services performed till the effective date of termination and any reasonable termination compensation for the unrecovered investments.
15.3 Termination of Agreement for Convenience

Customer may terminate this Agreement upon not less than ninety (90) days' notice to the Service Provider. However, this Agreement shall continue to remain in effect with respect to any Work Order already issued hereunder until such other Work Order is itself terminated and/or performance thereunder is completed.
15.4 Termination for Material Breach

In the event of a material breach of the provisions of this Agreement or an applicable Work Order, the non- breaching party may terminate this Agreement and all Work Order, or any individual Work Order and this Agreement as it applies to such Work Order, upon written notice to the breaching party if the breaching party fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days following receipt of written notice from the non-breaching party requiring the remedy.
15.5 Termination for Insolvency

Either party may terminate this Agreement or an applicable Work Order, in the event of any proceedings in bankruptcy, insolvency or winding up by or against the other party or for the appointment of an assignee or equivalent for the benefit of creditors or of a receiver or of any similar proceedings.
15.6 Survival:

The provisions of this Agreement necessary to interpret the respective rights and obligations of the parties hereunder or under any Work Order, shall so survive the termination of this Agreement or such Work Order. In addition, Customer shall remain obligated to pay Service Provider any amounts due hereunder for Services performed and expenses incurred under any Work Order.
16 Miscellaneous
16.1 Force Majeure

Either party shall be excused from delays in performing or from its failure to perform hereunder to the extent that such delays or failures result from causes beyond the reasonable control of such party; provided that, in order to be excused from delay or failure to perform, such party must act diligently to remedy the cause of such delay or failure.
16.2 No Agency

Service Provider, in rendering performance under Work Orders issued hereunder from time to time, is acting solely as an independent contractor. Customer does not undertake by this Agreement or otherwise to perform any obligation of Service Provider, whether by regulation or contract. In no way is Service Provider to be construed as the agent or to be acting as the agent of Customer in any respect, any other provisions of this Agreement or any Work Orders issued hereunder notwithstanding.
16.3 Multiple Counterparts
This Agreement may be executed in several counterparts, all of which taken together shall constitute one single Agreement between the parties.
16.4 Section Headings; Exhibits

The section and subsection headings used herein are for reference and convenience only, and shall not enter into the interpretation hereof. The exhibits referred to herein and attached hereto, or to be attached hereto, including all Work Orders issued hereunder from time to time, are incorporated herein to the same extent as if set forth in full herein.
16.5 Required Approvals
Where agreement, approval, acceptance, or consent by either party is required by any provision of this Agreement, such action shall not be unreasonably delayed or withheld.
16.6 No Waiver

No delay or omission by either party hereto to exercise any right or power occurring upon any noncompliance or default by the other party with respect to any of the terms of this Agreement shall impair any such right or power or be construed to be a waiver thereof. A waiver by either of the parties hereto of any of the covenants, conditions, or agreements to be performed by the other shall not be construed to be a waiver of any succeeding breach thereof or of any covenant, condition, or agreement herein contained. Unless stated otherwise, all remedies provided for in this Agreement shall be cumulative and in addition to and not in lieu of any other remedies available to either party at law, in equity, or otherwise.
16.7 Acts or omissions of Other Party

Neither Party shall be liable for any delay or failure in the performance of its obligations under this Agreement or any Work Order hereunder, if and to the extent such delay or failure is caused by the actions or omissions of the other Party or other Party's agents or due to a breach of this Agreement or a Work Order by the other Party.
16.8 Governing Law
The Agreement shall be governed in accordance with the laws of state of Missouri, USA.
16.9 Entire Agreement

This Agreement and the exhibits annexed hereto, together with the Work Orders issued from time to time hereunder, constitute the entire agreement between the parties. Each party acknowledges that it has not relied on or been induced to enter into this Agreement by a representation or warranty other than those expressly set out in this Agreement. To the extent permitted by applicable Law, a party is not liable to another party in contract or tort or in any other way for a representation or warranty that is not set out in this Agreement. No change, waiver, or discharge hereof shall be valid unless it is in writing and is executed by the party against whom such change, waiver, or discharge is sought to be enforced.
16.10 Order of Precedence
In the event of conflict between this Agreement and the exhibits annexed hereto, together with the Work Order issued from time to time hereunder, the following order of precedence would prevail:
1. Master Services Agreement
2. Exhibits
3. Work Order

The Parties agree that this Agreement and the applicable WO(s) will govern and supersede any terms and conditions stated on any purchase order or other ordering document submitted by Client, the terms of which, except for terms describing price and quantity, are null and void with respect to this Agreement, regardless of mutual execution of any purchase order at any time.
16.11 Publication/Advertising

Neither party shall use the other party's name or that of any of its divisions or affiliates or otherwise expressly or impliedly refer to any of them in any advertising, promotional literature, press release or other form of public disclosure without the prior written approval of the appropriate officer of that party. Any violation of this Section 16.11 shall be considered a material breach of this Agreement.
16.12 Insurance

Service Provider will secure, and maintain in force during the Term and for two (2) years thereafter, the following insurance policies, which shall name Customer as an additional insured: (a) commercial general liability, including bodily injury, property damage, owners and contractors protective liability, products and completed operations liability and contractual liability, with an annual per occurrence limit of not less than $1,000,000 and an annual general aggregate limit of not less than $2,000,000; (b) professional errors and omissions insurance in an annual amount of not less than $5,000,000 aggregate limit, and (c) cyber liability coverage with business interruption and data loss coverage of not less than $1,000,000 for each occurrence during any annual period, and an annual amount of $2,000,000 in the aggregate. Promptly upon request, Service Provider shall provide evidence of the foregoing insurance coverages.
16.13 Notices

Under this Agreement if one party is required to give notice to the other, such notice shall be deemed given if mailed by registered mail acknowledgement due or by email, and addressed as follows (or as subsequently noticed to the other party):

To Customer:
444 West 47<sup>th</sup> Street, Suite 900
Kansas City, Missouri 64112
Attn: General Counsel.

To Service Provider:
2035 Lincoln Highway, Suite 3000,
Edison Square West, Edison- NJ 08817.
Attn: Legal Dept.
16.14 No Assignment

Neither party may, without the prior written consent of the other party, assign or transfer this Agreement nor any obligation incurred hereunder, except by merger, reorganization, consolidation, or sale of all or substantially all of such party's assets. Any attempt to do so in contravention of this Section shall be void and of no force and effect.
16.15 Employee Non-Solicitation

Service Provider and Customer each agree that during the time that Service Provider personnel or Customer employees are associated with the Services hereunder and for a period of one (1) year after such person ceases to be so associated, neither Service provider nor Customer shall, directly or indirectly, knowingly solicit for hire or knowingly hire or retain the personnel of the other party as an employee or independent contractor or through a third party vendor or service provider, except with the prior written consent of the other party.
16.16 Dispute Settlement

This Agreement is entered into and shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflict of laws rules. Each Party hereby consents to the jurisdiction of state and federal courts in New York City, New York of any action to enforce or interpret this Agreement.
16.17 Severability
If any term or provision of this Agreement should be declared invalid by a court of competent jurisdiction, the remaining terms and provisions of this Agreement shall be unimpaired.
IN WITNESS THEREOF, Customer and Service Provider have caused this Agreement to be signed and delivered by their duly authorized officers, all as of the date first hereinabove written.
